title: Doesn’t track for me
body:
Got a message from streaks that I had not completed a task. I had but went in to check. Streaks said I had completed it as well. The next day streaks showed that I no longer had a streak. This has happened more than a few times. Checked the app on my phone and watch. Both said I had finished the task yet kept getting reminders and the next day it would say I had not completed the task. Sometimes both were in agreement, sometimes not. When not I would change the one that claimed I had not completed the task. Next morning, sometimes, the streak was zeroed out. Sometimes not. 

The app also does not track my watch well. I complete three rings and Streaks sometimes says I have not and the next day my streak is over. 

To a degree I don’t care if it keeps track of the streak. Part of my life is hard to predict and missing some tasks on certain days is necessary. That said, I like to reflect and and this glitch makes that impossible. I can’t know if it was the program or me. 

I do like how the app focuses my attention and helps to form habits. Entirely worth it for just that. Not sure what else is out there but Sreaks is far better than anything I have tried. That said I will keep looking while using this app or hope this issue stops for me.

title: Handy, but a few things I wish for
body:
This app has already helped me make progress on some streaks, but I wish a few things:

1. More streaks (unlimited groups). I get the minimalism, but some users eventually want to build even more habits without deleting old ones, or break them into smaller achievable steps which makes 12 insufficient. In a similar vein, unlimited groups would be useful for grouping habits by interval, like daily with daily, weekly with weekly, etc, regardless of total number of habits.

2. Archiving “completed” habits. Maybe some streaks are ready to retire, but someone who cares about achieving something like a 365-day streak probably hates to just delete it like it never existed to make room for a new one. Put the archived streakes at the end out of the way. More than 6 per page would be fine.

3. Better syncing with Apple watch. I’ve noticed that if I don’t open Streaks on my phone every day - it doesn’t detect whatever I recorded on the watch app. Then I have to manually “complete” any missed days on the phone app, which isn’t the most intuitive thing in the world.

title: Rough Start
body: I bought this app based on a rave review so I have the ‘pro’ version. While it is easy to get started for basic habit tracking, I remembered reading that it could be used like a Pomodoro task master which is what I now want it for because the existing ones are either too involved ‘to do’ type apps or simplistic timers. It took quite a while to wade through how to create tasks with adequate specificity because it takes numerous passes through editing a task because all the options are not present when you first set up a habit; you create a default habit and then edit the heck out of it to get to a scheduled habit of specific length with notification reminders. It also has weird language like when it specifies the number of times a day you want to perform a habit; instead of phrasing it that way, it says “number of days” when what it means is number of times during your specified time period (day, week, month), yet the previous three options are phrased correctly. I am pretty tech savvy and it took quite a bit of playing around with the app to figure things out, even with the help section. I guess I like words more than icons (hieroglyphics as we used to call them). This app could definitely benefit by on app instructions.

author: Viewer111

title: I love this, just like one more feature
body: I love this app! The idea of seeing your Streaks is very powerful. The icons and color themes are also so cute! However, it would be great if the app made you actively enter that you didn’t complete the task instead of just marking it complete. It’ll make me feel more guilty if the app actually makes me enter that I didn’t complete the task versus not doing anything and forgetting about it. Something like having to click “yes or no “each day. It would just be so powerful to enter no when I didn’t complete the task instead of not having to do anything and forgetting about the app
author: PinkCupcake11

title: Simple Customization
body: I use it daily. I repurpose buttons quickly as my workout changes. It is very easy to use.
author: Azrael13666dz

title: As a habit-forming app, fails at its main job of motivating you
body:
The design is unique. But is that design helpful? Does the app motivate you to maintain the streaks? Nope. 

As someone who wants to form habits or build a routine, this app felt like the perfect candidate, until you realize that it doesn’t even help you see your recent success with the different habits at a glance. 

Handling the advanced options is like playing with adult stuff as a child. You just poke here and there to figure out how things work. Button titles instead of ambiguous icons would help. 

On the other hand, there a few silly features like a ton of app icons you can choose from, and lots of other customizations. 

Unsure how it won an Apple Design Award!
author: LazyChap

title: Excellent app but with minor bugs

author: VAHID88

title: brilliant
body: this app appeals to competitor in all of us, in the best way possible!  all it takes is a few days in a row of accomplishing a small task - nothing overwhelming at all - and i was hooked into not wanting to lose my streak! 👍 my only point of criticism is what time the 24 “day” starts - midnight. i’m a night owl and am often up until 12:30 or so and i can’t always record what i did that day because it falls after the midnight mark when goals have been reset. i would love to be able to customize this time i choose for a 24 hour period to coincide better with my schedule. otherwise, we’ll done!

author: cbboots

title: Awesome app, 1 issue
body:
I’m loving the app. It’s a clever way to incentivize the things you care about in a clean, easy to use way. 

The only annoyance I am having is that the status of all the streaks resets at midnight. This is a problem for things like staying under a calorie goal or flossing at night, because you might not finish the item until after midnight. This is a particular problem for night owls like myself. It would be great if you could define your normal day separator as being something like 3 am to avoid these boundary condition issues.

author: OMJ170

title: A Life changing app!!!
body:
You can choose up to 12 habits, pick the frequency per day/week.  It counts how long your streaks are in performing the habit making one want to continue so the streak isn’t broken.  It syncs really well to the Apple Watch.  For example, if you set your step goal at 12,000, the app will tell you how many steps you have left to reach that goal.

This app has me doing things I was having a really difficult time getting myself to do.  I have also paired this with reducing mindless phone use, so I am not allowed to play with the phone until all of my Streak items have been accomplished.  Life changing.

author: majeske

title: Best habit forming app I’ve used
body: I’ve used several different habit tracking apps and I ha r to say that the simplicity of Streaks makes it number 1.  I’ve been using it for about a year now and it has helped me build habits of daily mindfulness (connected with the Breathe app and Health to automatically log in Streaks), 7+ hrs of sleep each night, and more.  Thank you, developers, for an app that is making a positive difference in my daily life!
author: _btp

title: Lacks critical function
body:
Lacks ability to reward for cumulative work over period of a week or two weeks when time spent each day varies day by day and week by week. 

A simple “complete the circle in X days, doesn’t matter you you do it” function would solve this and open up a lot possibility. Divide a task into pieces, complete X pieces in X days, and get rewarded along the way for each piece completed. Set alerts they way you want during that time period. 

Problem with this is the app currently wants you to assign PRECISELY the number of times per day you’re going to do something. That’s great for clock-punchers or those with regular routines. Doesn’t work for those with highly variable, unpredictable schedules. 

If there’s way to do this I’d love to know.
author: virtualEL

title: Frustrating bug
body: When it works it’s great- when it doesn’t it’s frustrating. That makes sense of course because the app has one job- one. If you complete a task but forget to mark it completed the app will fortunately allow you to mark it the next day. However IF you try to mark a task that requires multiple check ins (to be considered completed) the day after it’ll reset your streak. For example walking the dogs multiple times a day requires multiple check ins. If you forget on one day to check it in despite not missing the actual task you should be able to “mark it complete” the next day. But for what ever reason any task that involves multiple check ins will reset even if you “mark as complete for yesterday” putting you at one.

body: I don't know how this app won a design award from Apple. The concept is great, and it looks okay, but in terms of how it works -- it's a mess. The settings are so buried and obfuscated. The scheduling of tasks is broken. If you want to do something once a week, the data it provides is unintelligible. Lots of potential here but a ton of flaws as well.

title: Good app with an extremely unintuitive UI
body:

Multiple pages instead of continuous scroll is another problem. 
Took me about 3-5 mins to understand how to edit a task.
Note that I'm neither technologically impaired nor am I new to iOS ux patterns. It's just that most of us don't want to learn new patterns for the sake of one app.

That said, this is a very useful app for forming habits. And if you're reading this review, don't let it dissuade you from purchasing it. Just be aware of the UI kinks.

So unless you restore your phone backup, which I as a habit don’t, then you have to rely on the manual export import option. This would be a five-star app if that feature was added.

title: Well Designed to Develop Good Habits
body:
Streaks is well designed to help set goals for new habits and track your progress. The tasks can be customized to fit your exact goal and frequency. It only allows for six goals to be tracked so it’s not going to work for multi-task projects or a standard to-do list. Instead it’s built to help develop a few good habits at a time (e.g. walk 3 miles every Tuesday and Thursday, go to the gym three times a week, and stand up from my desk once an hour on weekdays). 

It’s very motivating to be able to mark a task complete and see the ‘streak’ number increase as I start meeting that goal more consistently. And if I’m not meeting a goal there’s no build up of incomplete to-do tasks. Intuitive reminders help remind me of the goals I’ve set and I can quickly get an overview of how many times I’ve completed a task. It’s a beautiful design with smart functionality to help me get more of what I want in my life.

title: Tricky to get into, but rewarding and customizable
body:
I bought this app after a user had stated they had achieved surprising weight goals. The biggest set back for me is procrastinating and not keeping track of my daily tasks. 

At first I was excited to set it up and test out the functionality. However, when I started using the app it was cumbersome to open each time I wanted to record a behavior. In the search/quick menu the UI buttons were small so when pressing them in vibrate mode I sometimes complete an entire multipart task instead of just the single part. There are no title separators for the icons so you had to think about the classifications and identify what groups they are yourself, this leads to searching for a while before you get through it. 

 This aside, once you get used to the UI the app is very customizable which is enjoyable. You can select multiple color schemes, icons and even the home screen app badge can be modified. The 12 tasks keep the measuring manageable, but I find that the streak is no more than a remainder. There is a sense of urgency to keep your streak going. However, I would love it if I could assign my own personal rewards for keeping a streak. This way the streak becomes more meaningful.

Great job guys, credit where it’s due. This app could change your life if you use it right. Worth the money.

This is doubly annoying when trying to view stats because you have to look at each screen individually. Graphs don’t really tell you anything. Seems designed to look nice in a preview but not really function efficiently. title: Simple and Effective.
body:
This is one of those apps that can actually make your life better. Over the past 30 days, it has helped me become more active, mindful, and disciplined.  I customize most of my streaks but I use a few preset ones too. 

For me, the key is to embrace the imperfection. I just see how high I can get my streak before breaking it. Then I try to go higher the next time. Don’t get discouraged by or try to justify a broken streak. Just beat it the next time around. 

I set the goal to pray and meditate daily. I made it 25 days until I broke my streak. No matter. I will make it at least 26 days this time. I set a goal not to use fowl language at work (with FIVE allowable slip-ups) and I haven’t made it past two days. 😂 Some streaks are going to be easier than others. I’ll get there though. 

Get this app. Use it! Beat your own records! Be better one streak at a time!!!

title: Perfect for tracking goals
body:
Love the simplicity of this tool. I use it to track my health goals (I.e.#of consecutive days without sugar, #of exercise sessions etc) and it's really helped me to stay on track. 

It's taken out a lot of my black and white thinking around my goals and I'm much happier with incremental progress. For instance, I may not be sugar free everyday, but I enjoy seeing that I'm 80% sugar free this month which is 10% better than last month. I now have real data to show me I'm moving in the direction of my goals, even if it I don't do things perfectly. 

Here are my top favorite things about it: 
1. Intuitive, uncluttered interface 
2. Ease of adding goals/targets 
3. It's rewarding to watch the wheel turn with each successful streak
4. Reminders are helpful
5. The exporting feature to track streak data over extended amounts of time.

title: Habits with a focus on simplicity
body:
Update for version 3:
This app jumped to 5 stars with its feature-rich enhancements and second screen, now allowing a dozen tracked items. I can throw my health-related goals (drink water, meditate, etc.) in one screen and my life-quality goals (e.g. Journal, Read 15 minutes, etc.) in another! And the customizations are fantastic - from the ability to change the App's springboard icon to its color-coded screens. Another very impressive update.

---

- what follows is a past review for version 2:
This app isn't suited for everyone wanting to form new habits, and for me it sits alongside "Balanced" app.

What's to like:
- It has large, simple icons in a minimalistic interface that keeps you focused on 6 core habits you want to keep track of.
- It ties into the health app so that it seamlessly checks off if you've met that health requirement for the day (e.g. Walk 5000 steps)
- It has multiple views that allow you to view you streak ratio and calendar.
- It has export functionality
- It ties to your Apple Watch

What could be improved
- You can't undo or edit historical data. If you accidentally sign off on the wrong item or - say - grab some cookies right before bed, thus invalidating your "only eat good food" goal, you can't revert.
- You can't import. This might just be the nature of having a minimalistic interface.
- You're limited to only six habits, though that might be a good thing if you're focusing on forming core habits. For people who want to monitor their day-to-day and weekly activities, Streaks will fall short. I use other programs to supplement this one and put 6 important goals in this app that I think are more necessary for my wellbeing - again, why I really like it tying to the health app.

Suggestion to users: pick six main goals that will support core habits that you want to achieve daily. Have one that's easy to achieve nearly every day but that you know you need (e.g. Eat breakfast) then three that are physical fitness oriented and two that are emotionally and mentally driven. Studies show that forming a regular health regimen acts as a catalyst to support other desirable changes in our lives. Use a different app to track all the other items if you want, but keep a minimalistic app like Streaks around to keep up with the core habits.

title: Effectively Simple, but Needs Something…
body:
You don't need fluff, billions of statistics, or a million features; just a simple counter and reminder app.  So far, Streak's simplicity and ease of use upgraded it to my first page of apps within one day of use.

That said, Streaks is standalone. It does not support syncing across multiple devices, and there is no native iPad support. This type of app lends itself to being accessible everywhere you see a screen, and the lack of syncing or native iPad support is a glaring hole in its elegantly minimal feature set.

Other than this, it's a useful tool that is satisfying to use. It encourages good habits and makes me want to improve myself every time I look at it. Its widget panel and Apple Watch app make it more easily accessible, but completing the circle with device syncing would be amazing.

title: Filling circles is fun!
body:
When I looked at habit-forming apps back in 2016, I didn't even consider Streaks [$4, iOS]. This is because the app limited you to six habits you could track. No premium, in-app purchase would increase or remove that limit.

After habit building for the past year, though, I've come to agree with the app's developer: trying to concentrate on more than six habits at a time is difficult. They wisely chose this limit to help users focus.

Or maybe it's because only six rings fit comfortably on one screen. Streaks' unique interface has you tap and hold on a habit to indicate completion; a cute animation completes the ring and fills in the circle to show your progress. The app uses the same UI on its Today widget, offering a super quick method for tracking your progress.

Frankly, those two features make Streaks the easiest of these apps to use and the most fun. But I still find some downsides to using the app.

One is that the app is just willy-nilly with its reminders. You can't set what times *you* want to be reminded of your habit; instead, the app remind you whenever *it* feels like it. Another is the lack of tracking for negative habits, those which you want to break. And while you *can* track habits that require multiple completions per day, you can't log the number of completions above a set amount; for example, I can't track how many times I sent a card above my goal of two times a day. Finally, there is no way to skip a day without breaking a streak.

But if these issues don't matter to you (and, for many, they won't) or if you like the idea of auto completing habits that are Health-related, Streaks is a fine app.

title: AMAZING APP, ONE SUGGESTION
body: I usually don't give ratings but I absolutely love this app! It's great for visually being able to see how you've been holding up on your personal habits, and does a great job by holding you accountable. You're definitely going to want those streaks going on as long as possible. I've only had this app for about 4-5 days, and it's helping me to build habits out of things I've been procrastinating on doing for months. My only suggestion to enhance this app would be the ability to choose the time of day that the app resets for the next day. Basically, you have until 11:59pm each day to knock out your habits or you'll lose your streak, which forces you to mark it as done before 11:59 and just make a personal promise to yourself to get it done before bed. Sometimes you may not have time to complete everything before then. So I think being able to set the time that the habits reset for the day will be crucial, for the sake of not being forced to accomplish everything in such a rigid timeframe.

title: Simple and beautiful, but also powerful
body:
Streaks is a simple app that lets you track 6 habits. With an easy tap you can mark something as done, and then see how you've been doing on it in the past.

title: Needs more than 6 goals
body:
This is my favorite app for keeping track of pesky behaviors one wants to improve. It is easy to use, and very important to me, graphically very cool. An app that is graphically pleasing actually makes me want to check in and use it several times a day. And when one completes all of them in a day, they turn from white to gold. Seems like a small thing, but it is motivating.   Many of the other such apps in the store don't pass that bar with their confusing layout. 
     The one big drawback of this app is that it only allows 6 goals. I find I am more successful when I break down a goal into smaller tasks. I am working on an ongoing doctor approved daily goal of changing to a whole foods plant based diet and eliminating sugar from my diet. Also I am trying to include different types of exercise in my day: strength, cardio, balance and meditation.  
I need positive feedback throughout the day to succeed. Using one goal for "Eat Healthy Today" doesn't work for me, rather I need 5 goals, one devoted to each meal and for snacks along with a separate reminder goal of No Sweets.  With only one goal left, there isn't enough to 3 types of exercise plus daily meditation. 
     I recognize the thinking behind having just a few goals to focus on, but for those of us who need to break it down into smaller goals, 6 just isn't enough.
     It would be nice to have 12, A Daily Dozen. To keep the graphic integrity of the app, perhaps the 12 could be on two pages, 6 per page. This would solve the problem that 12 might lead to graphic clutter if all on one page. For those users for which 6 is enough, one wouldn't have to ever swipe to page 2. But for those of us who need more, a simple swipe would allow us to have the flexibility we need to be truly successful in establishing new habits.

Note 3-15-17: I originally gave 3 stars to this app, not on function or design which deserves 5 stars, but solely based on the limitation of only 6 goals. I also wrote to the app designer.  I quickly received a friendly response saying that they are already working on expanding the number of goals to a second page of 6.  For this immediate, positive feedback from the designer I have added a well-deserved 4th star.

title: Simplistic, Easy to Use, Easy to Forget
body:
I recommend this app if you're looking to create and install new, good habits into your lifestyle. There's a few things you'll need to do, and there's a couple of important ways they can improve this app.

You'll need to take a few minutes and set out customized reminders for your goals so you don't forget about them. These help, but for me they don't show up everyday or consistently. I don't know if this is a bug, but I've checked all of my notification settings. I need these to show up on my lock screen or Notification Center more liberally, perhaps even annoyingly, or else I'll forget about these habits I'm trying to work on.

One thing I recommend for new users of this app is to add it to their main home screen front and center where you'll see it multiple times each day. That'll make it a little harder to forget, even if the app doesn't send you those important reminders you wanted.

Edit: I've since followed Streaks on twitter and I wanted to add a star here because this developer is doing superb work. They actually support the app consistently, and add updates for 3D Touch and Notification Center features. I absolutely recommend this app!

title: Amazingly useful
body:
This app is really amazing.  I have been using it for a couple of months, tracking some things I want to do for myself (and for others), but don't usually do because I run out of willpower by the end of the day or just don't put my own needs ahead of other responsibilities.  Using this app changed that! I have been lifting weights, doing cardio, playing with my poor lonely cats, cleaning their water fountain, and cleaning their litter box.  I did each of these things before using this app, but it was sporadic and wholly unpredictable.  Now I (typically) do these things the number of times I defined for each task each week, and I feel great!  I've lost twenty pounds and my cats appear much happier!

At first I thought that having only six items you can track would be limiting, but as time went on I realized that I'm insanely busy, and that's why I often don't do what I intend on doing.  Keeping the number of goals small keeps it within reach.  I've typically tried to make a dozen changes all at once but have never succeeded.  I am succeeding now, and now that the gym has become habit (and even enjoyable), I'm going to remove it from Streaks and add a couple other small goals.

This is a really great app, well done, attractive, bug-free, useful, and simple. Paired with a kaizen model of small, incremental change, I consider this app the single most important tool on my phone.

title: Phenomenal App with Great Customer Service
body:
It's simple (up to 6 tasks and that's it!). It's intuitive. It's lightweight. It's beautiful. 

But then something happened in the last update. They got rid of the ability to stop health related completed notifications. Now I don't know about you, but I really cherished the silence as those notifications didn't do anything for me. If you're not familiar with the notifications, the tasks that link to the health app can trigger a notification that tells you they've been completed. But between you and me? They're useless. Why? Because you can't do anything from it. There's no action. If anything, you'll stop being active since you've completed your daily task. It's just not actionable and it's bothersome to get alert fatigue. So I emailed the developers!

They responded immediately. 

And guess what? They brought back the feature to turn them off in this update! It wasn't more than two weeks ago that I emailed them asking to bring it back that they acted upon it. They understood my qualms about alert fatigue and actionable notifications and they quickly reversed course by adding the ability to turn those notifications off. This has been the most joyful interaction I've ever had with an app developer. These guys really command an amazing ship and I wish the best for them. They're quick, smart, and great developers. And their app reflects that. 

Way to go guys! You exceeded my every expectation - so much so that I'm writing this review. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you!

Unfortunately I'm going to move onto another app because they limit you on only being able to track and work on six things at a time. I get that having too many things you are working on will most likely lead to failure, but when you have lots of new habits you want to make in your life, as you start accomplishing some and want to add others it's nice to be able to still track how you are doing in the previous ones. I really wish they created space that you could swip thru to other pages and keep six per page but not limit us on our goals or what we want to track. Plus I have goals I want to track for different areas of my life and would love to be able to group them together. 

I hope they change this, but until they do it's mostly useless to me. Very sad about that!

title: Simple, Well-Executed, Excellent
body: I've tried many habits apps before this one. A list maker by nature, every activity from staying healthy to tracking homework assignments made its way onto some list app of mine. That said, I've not loved any of those more than Streaks. In it, I'm able to keep track of a *few* things that I *should* do every day while not overwhelming myself with a flood of tasks. Because of its limits on the number of trackable activities, I'm able to focus on habitually completing a small set of truly important activities each day. Its GUI is simple and flat yet perfectly sharp; complexity is not its virtue, but conciseness. I would highly recommend this app to anyone (but especially the busy at heart or the workaholic) wishing to adopt a set of daily standards unwavering for circumstances. I don't rate apps often (I haven't since I rated Civilization V on the Mac App Store), but this is a great one.

title: Simple Idea, Well Executed
body:
Some of the best iOS apps are the ones that don't try to do too much. Streaks is one of those apps. It has a nice interface, and it does what you ask it to and then gets out of your way.

I like that it's smart enough to know that, even though I've told it that I work out on every day except Monday, if I *do* happen to work out on a Monday, that gets added to my streak.

I also like the flexible way it handles notifications. I can set custom notifications for each of my items. 

And, the Watch app actually works! A rare treat, indeed. 

If you're the type of person who is motivated by that idea of checking off an item on a checklist every day, you will love this app. I'm that type of person, and my workout and creative writing routines have been recharged in the four months I've been using Streaks.

title: Clean, simple, and effective!

It isn't easy to find that balance of creating an app that is so easy to use and so well done in a category that is already quite busy. I've tried other apps that worked toward the goal of creating good habits, but they suffered from a complicated design or a lack of intuitive control. This has both, and I'm already hooked. I hope to come back and edit my review in a few weeks to report how well it does continuing to reinforce good habit formation, and studies indicate it takes at least 3 weeks for them to properly form. Here's to a better life through more consistent behaviors. Kudos!

title: Beautiful, usable, simple
body:

While it's difficult to focus on all six at once, I can build momentum from one or two successful streaks and expand to the others. I'm a writer and grad student, and I would especially recommend this app to creative professionals, minimalists, and anyone who needs a little help focusing on goals.

My only disappointment is that the history goes back no further than the previous month if you've been spotty (ie not on a streak). On the one hand I guess that's a good motivation to keep a streak going; on the other, I'm losing trackable data that could help me fine-tune my approach. title: It's okay
body:
This app has you put in six activities you'd like to do by day. You can customize the combination as well as change the color of the back ground. It's simple with a minimalist design. It's also easy to use. 

But the bottom line is I paid for a check list. You hold down the circles to mark off a task as completed. If you don't do it, it'll send you notifications. If you're someone serious about forming a habit and need your phone to remind you, then it may be worth the money. For me, it was nothing special. 

Be aware the app is what you make of it. It won't magically motivate you or reward you. It's just there as a reminder and keep track of what tasks you've completed. Before you drop the money, really decide if this will benefit your life. It's like a naggy spouse you can turn off, defeating the purpose.

body:
The features of this app are really limited for what it is and the reminders are super annoying.  

There is a limited number of habits that it allows you to track which would be understandable for a free app but not something i pay for. 

Also it only allows you to mark a task as done or not which for habits like drinking 8 glasses of water a day is ridicules. You should be able to mark of each glass of water after you drink it instead of trying to remember how many you had at the end of the day. 

Also the reminders are set up to go off one right after the other, so if you have 6 habits you're tracking it will remind you of each one, one at a time, a couple of seconds a part. This is super annoying when your phone just starts going off at night. 

It would be great if it could also provide analytics for your habits. That way you could better identify what might be preventing you from reaching your goals. 

Ok app but far from being worth money.

title: Good not great Don't break the chain
body:
Summary - expensive for what it is - after the intrusive bold block color wears off you're left with a ui that's lacking  a big rewarding calendar or charts with bright or a well functioning watch app. The app also tells me apparently I shouldn't trying build mire than six habits with this arbitrary list limit. What if I wanted to do one thing per day? Out of luck.  

I've sent email to support and I will update my rating and review when the things I mentioned are addressed. Unfortunately right now this app is not really worth recommending.  

The long
---/
The core function is fine if very limited and on the iPhone they use tiny graphs and charts in laying the original circle icon but in the watch app you can't see the same information. In fact the watch app does virtually nothing except allow you to click done or not.   And to do that you go into the app.  Then see a display of all your items. Then tap one of them to go in. Then tap again to mark done.  Why not just allow mark done on the first screen? Also the taps register very very very poorly. Sometimes not at all and sometimes delayed three or four seconds.  Having just reloaded my Apple Watch and confirming all other apps work more speedily now this is an app specific issue. The tiny calendars is a really big error given this is a don't break the chain app.  Also No complication or glance or chart view. 

I hope to see these shortcomings rectified.  They're on the right track just missing a few things I find key.

title: Supremely good
body:
Streaks is the best way to develop a habit. The idea isn't to stuff it with to-dos or expected chores, but to choose tasks that you want to develop a habit for, and gradually, as days go by, they become part of your routine and you wouldn't need a reminder for them. And when that happens, you replace those newly formed habits with newer aspirations.

An as example, one of my tasks is "Read one New Yorker essay" set on a daily basis. The goal of this task is to get me to check my NYR subscription on a daily basis and dig into my past issues. Instead of trying to read the issues as they come out (which is incredibly difficult, and impossible for me personally) I'd read one essay per day, from any issue. Another task I have is "Read 50 pages", which I don't count my NYR essay toward. Thus, I want to develop a habit of reading (daily) through my own books, as well as catching up with relevant issues and reporting from my favorite publication. The app would nudge me every day (just once) toward that goal, reminding me to put my free time into these goals.

It's an effective way for me to be reminded of the simple pleasures or aspirations that I wish I can sustain. And it works surprisingly well.

title: Love this!!
body: I'm a grown up with responsibilities and expectations... But my little ADHD self STILL forgets to brush my teeth at night. I can put on a production with 50 people for 300 people to watch, but I forget to eat a healthy meal. Streaks helps me with the day to day habits I struggle with. It also really helps to build new habits. It takes me years to pick up new habits. Plus, since it counts how many times you've done it in a row, it totally plays on my competitive nature. I have gotten out of bed to brush my teeth just because I didn't want to lose my streak. I would be giving it a 5, except sometimes I accidentally put a habit as being done and it's difficult to undo it once you've marked it done. It that was easier to alter, I'd give this a 5!

title: Motivating app!
body:
Streaks is a great, easy to use app. I find that I am motivated to do things on my list--and it's not easy to motivate me! I often fall short on completing goals, but something about "circling" it off in Streaks has helped me to finish some tasks. And if you're not able to complete the task as you've set up, it actually prompts you to set a more realistic goal! 👍🏻 
As other reviewers have said, my schedule is so variable, that I really wish I could change the day of the week easier, or just say that I want to do something 3 times a week, and then choose the day myself. That's my only complaint, and why I gave it 4 stars instead of 5.

The newest addition of the ability to choose number of times per week is really great too! For example I don't have a set schedule for exercising but I'd like to exercise 3 times per week, so now I can add that in streaks! The only thing that could make this app better is to add more tasks. Maybe the developers have a reason for only having six, but otherwise it doesn't seem hard to either allow us to flip to the next page for more or scroll down. Adding pages by category would be cool. One page for your health tasks, a page for school or work tasks, etc. or just let users name their own pages.

title: Straight and to the point.
body:

2.) Would like the ability to set specific days for tasks. For example, limit work tasks to only Mon-Fri.
3.) Would like to see a list view of tasks to check when I'm on my iPhone versus the circle method (which is great on the Apple Watch)
4.) would like the reporting on the device to be a little more robust. So far everything is in a calendar timeline. Would like bar, line, pie graphs as well as the ability to filter by day of the week, etc.

Other than that nicely designed.

title: Really good at what it's aiming at
body:
This is a great motivational tool! It is intended to focus you on your most important goals. So you will have to make some decisions. 
First: you are limited to 6 goals. If you have more than 6 "most important goals" you will have to rethink your life. Don't blame the App. 
Second: You can pick day of the week that you want to achieve something. But if you just want to check that you've done something, let's say, 3 times a week, this is not your app. It is called Streaks for a reason: if you don't need to do it regularly, you don't need to track it here. 
Lastly, if you need to track something that you need to do more than once a day (like brushing your teeth), you can just hit complete after you did it the last time. Because that's when you've accomplished your goal. Surely, you can count to 3?
The interface is beautiful in its simplicity. I hope they don't give in to those who request more "fine tuning." And I love the somewhat hidden feature of making a completion count for the day before. Because I frequently forget to check off my goals at the end of the day. 
Thank you for a simple yet well designed App!!

body: This app has helped motivate me do build good habits. I wasn't sure it would make a difference but it turns out I really dislike breaking my streaks. Like other reviewers I think the app would be even better with a function for tracking tasks done multiple times a day. Also it would be nice to be able to add more than six tasks. Overall though, this is a simple, useful app.

body:
Sorry guys, but I have more than 6 tasks in a day to focus on. It was an awesome app until I had to stop at 6! 😩
Until there's a fix for that, this app is an instant delete.
author: Samantha8802

title: Love it but..
body: There should be more than just 6 tasks.. otherwise I love it:)
author: Devind20

author: Haniisauce

title: Excellently Simple
body: It works because it's minutely focused in a totally customizable way. Already changing my habits for the better!
author: AmyDRobinson

title: Clean UI, easy to use
body: Very clean to look at, easy to use, and really makes me realize how many important things I say I'll get around to but never actually do.

title: Love it.
body: Great app

body:
It has been five days that I started using this app, and I am already seeing changes in how I apportion my time to activities I consider key to every day. 

My only feature request is an ability to mark an activity as complete without opening the app. A widget for the notifications pull down would be one way to accomplish this.

author: chococat12!

author: KaijaLove

title: Gentle reminder
body: I really like this app. When I open my phone it shows me what I need to complete for the day.
author: Rankirsch

title: Motivational and Easy
body: Great app. I also enjoy the flexibility with the icons.  Wouldn't mind if you could track more than 6 items though. But outside if that I am enjoying using it to stay on track.
author: DAvellanet

title: Would like to have more tasks
body:
Nice idea and will help with discipline of follow through but would like to see more tasks instead of just 6. 
Thanks
author: Dutchcoffeenut

title: Nope
body: The icons are cool but I've used other habit tracker apps that I liked better. My biggest issue with this one is that I haven't found a way to go back a change the previous day. If I forget to mark my habit before midnight, it counts it as not done. That doesn't work for me
author: SamAustin

title: Motivating
body: I got this app free from Starbucks and I've been using it for a couple weeks now. It definitely has made me strive to complete my task but I am not sure I'll continue to be as motivated. Also I wish I could track more than six things.
author: Mizzcrys

title: Cool one
body: I would like to be able to add more tasks
author: Palina17

title: Someone wrote "quiet motivation"
body: And I completely agree. Simple yet powerful little app. Can't wait to see what improvements and enhancements the writers add over time.
author: bradyb23

title: Excellent! ...what's next?
body: This is an excellent app! At present, it is a beautiful way to record certain kinds of activities and it displays progress, motivates, and rewards the user. Of course, there are functionalities that need to be added. What about counting items that happen more than once? What about adding measurable data upon completion? I hope this beautiful app continues to grow!
author: coffeeandtoast

title: Simple and Effective
body: I'm normally really bad with keeping up with things. This app is great at helping me remember to do small, good habit forming tasks such as studying or walking a certain distance. I like how can I set certain tasks for certain days of the week. Overall I am very impressed and hopeful that this app can keep me on a good track!
author: miggs94

title: So far so good
body: Have been tracking custom goals and works good.. Would recommend that the notification tag only come up AFTER the time passes
author: Emaillesw

title: Helpful Habits
body:
This app is helping me build good habits. It helps create a little competition with myself to make sure I take enough time in the day for a few goals - it is satisfying to have all the dots filled in and numbers go up! 
I plan on adding more tasks as the weeks go by to help organize my typically unscheduled and undisciplined life.
author: kikicooley

title: Very Kind
body: I like how you can leave streaks for the previous day if you were too tired to open the app or forgot to mark it complete. A kindly reminder app.
author: Jack Cloverway

title: Great app for tracking goals
body: It's motivating to see the streak build.
author: carol0626

title: Good motivator
body:
I really like this app and how you can customize it. It is a good motivator, but I wish there could be more than 6 tasks...though I understand that the point is to focus on a few tasks. 
Overall great app!
author: TrinaGirl42

title: Awesome App, Needs more Slots
body: Really cool and it adds a bit of fun getting to continue my streak every day! Helps you build habits. It only has 6 slots for tasks, though - I could have easily put in 20.
author: lanceworley

title: It's on you!
body: For those few things u can di to promote good health, this is a way to have a daily conversation with yourself!
author: Teegeew

title: Love it!
body: I love this app! I sometimes have trouble remembering everything, but with Streaks it is so easy. User- friendly and motivational. I would totally recommend you get this
author: oliviaales

title: I actually like it, but....
body:
I actually enjoy this app. If there was one thing I would change about it, I would make it so that there were sub categories. I make goals for my health, finances, spiritual health, household chores, and goals that I am working on. I'd like to have a way to track my habits in each category. 
But I do enjoy this app and would recommend it to others.
author: Mrs Tilsy

title: Love it!
body: Beautiful was to stay motivated!
author: JoelKrypton

title: Very motivating!
body: It's a great, gentle reminder to do six tasks each day (or however often you want to do them).  Five of my tasks are daily and watering the plants is a few times a week. I sometimes wish I could add more than six tasks, but otherwise it's really helpful and easy to use!
author: HollyGoLightly54

title: It is a great reminder to do the things most important to me!
body: Great idea
author: Steve 0369

title: Cool app
body: I'm always looking for ways to incorporate healthy habits into my life. This app will definitely help me do that.
author: allik3929

title: 5 Stars
body: Simple. Elegant. Helpful. Fun. Great Apple Watch integration. Keep up the good work.

title: Great app for keeping track of daily tasks
body: Great app for keeping track of daily tasks

title: Nice
body: Simple, easy to use
author: Fireman7804

author: Tylor Goodson

author: Aed7714

title: Excellent!!
body: Helps me get everything that I need done! Also it's great for teens so parents don't have to remind them to do their chores or any other responsibilities! Plus it is great motivation!

body: Love the app

title: Streakmaster
body: This helps me stay on track witch my daily goals!
author: TiaMia63

title: Helps form good habits

author: VeronicaRose922

title: Satisfying
body: I love the quite motivation and personal set up. I use it for the small stuff that is separate from work, relationships, or errands. Small items that help remind me to take some time to slow down. It's really nice about me missing a day too! I'm glad I'm using it.
author: Rachel umm

title: Lifesaver!!
body: Absolutely perfect for me! It keeps track of tasks I need to do and does it in a way where it's oddly motivating! Plus the fact that it works with the Heath app is nice too. Great layout for making goals and accomplishing them!!
author: Bsdbjkvsdvhj

title: Does the job
body: Simple reminder to help you build a habit. Keeps me accountable with my goals.
author: Mimisweb

title: I love this app!
body: This app really helps you become more accountable to yourself.
author: bendhall

title: Good app
body: I got this free from Starbucks and use it as a reminder to take meds and vitamins as well do chores. So far, it is very helpful.
author: Creative Writing Fan

title: Great reminders
body: Great app for gentle reminders that aren't annoying. If you're having trouble remembering things use this app! You can set up custom reminder times for each of your six items. So you can remind yourself just at the right time. The  Watch app works nicely. It's simple and straight forward.
author: 911tothecore

title: A friendly reminder
body:
It is so cool to be able to have an active reminder. It's fun to play a game to see if you can accomplish your tasks for the day. Makes one want to do them if only to keep the streak alive! 
Just wish I could add a few more reminders. Would be nice to have the option. I have just started using this app and haven't found anything wrong with it yet.
author: ChoosingMe2

title: Great reminder and motivational app!
body: Simple interface and great idea that builds off of Apple's Activity app! If there is a way to show rings similar to the activity app on the Apple Watch complication that would be great.
author: The Pianoman

title: Good App, Needs Improvement
body: It's a high quality app that offers quiet motivation and a clean interface. Very useful. The only issues are that it only allows up to six tasks (really unhappy with the fact that the makers think they know what's best for me), and that you can't do tasks more than once a day (like brushing teeth). If they could fix these things it would be excellent!
author: Amy Garrison

title: Great app but could use more features
body: I would love if there was a widget option so that I don't have to open the app continuously. Also if there was a way to add partially completed circles (i.e. Drink 8 glasses of water a day, you can tap for 1/8 the circle every time you drink one glass to keep track) and also if there were more features that connected to the Health app.
author: alimx0008

title: Awesome
body: Love the simplicity especially for the Apple Watch. Most apps try to hard to do too much and this app found the right amount of functionality and usability. I love the animations and it gives you an oddly nice sensation when you complete a streak for the day.
author: Zachscpowell

title: Task limits
body: Really unhappy with the limit of only six tasks a day.  I don't like the fact that someone else who does not know me or the way my brain works thinks that I would do better focusing on six tasks at a time. I really need something that starts with 10 or 20. Then they can max it at that. Or perhaps make a way for you to earn an extra task spot as you complete your tasks. Yeah, I like that idea better. Give my brain an incentive.
author: Amypk4

title: Could be so much more
body:
It's almost good. 

It lacks the ability to add more than six tasks. And it needs more customizations like adding more sets to one task. So if you have a task that is repeated through out the day it's not recorded if it's not something like walking or running.

I really like the concept and the interface and how easy it is to mark something completed.

It just narrowly missed the mark on being more fully featured and flexible in customizing and adding tasks.
author: eleven12music

title: Great idea- 1 suggestion
body: I have a goal of drinking 10 8oz waters (or 5 .5l bottles) per day.  Is it possible to set the app up to easily record each completed bottle and fill the check after all are completed?
author: Stuey713

title: Clean, simple, easy, limited.
body: I'd like to be able to split goals into multiple parts, for example: if I wanted to eat three servings of fruit per day, I could mark each individual fruit instead of my entire goal at once. I would also like the ability to set more than six goals.
author: Captain Rob

title: Quiet motivation!
body: I love this app because it's unobtrusive, but filling the circle and seeing the number go up motivates me to keep a streak going as long as possible, even when I'm having a low spoons day. Like another reviewer has said, it would be nice if you could track something you need to do multiple times a day and each hold would stop to fill part of the circle. Then again, that would probably require an accommodation like making a separate page to slide to for "daily multiple tasks," and one of the most pleasing parts of this app is its simple and clean style.
author: meringuefluff

title: Incredibly effective
body: Great idea. Great implementation. Use it primarily on my watch. Bravo!
author: Htowner

title: Helps you hold yourself accountable
body: Great for motivation, design, and visualizing progress. Simple and well designed. Excited to see where this goes next.
author: Shplr

title: Good not great
body: I like the icons, and the simplicity. It would be nice to have streaks also when I've been doing something 3x a week. Not all habits need to be done daily
author: Harvarddesi

title: does what it says
body: syncs and tracks and looks shiny and sometimes motivates reinforcement of defined behaviours and/or a hopefully self-perpetual completionism within oneself.
author: auto_logic

title: Smart, simple & efficient
body: Clean, slick visuals paired with a simple, intuitive interface makes for a vey efficient app that encourages you to track a few habits. Does the job for me!👍🏼👍🏼
author: Rob Sketcherman

title: Use it constantly
body: I use this app on my Apple Watch constantly. It reminds me in flexible ways to do things and helps me build good habits. I look forward to new features they surely will add over time. I've been using it for 3 weeks.
author: Hedonistic Bohemian

title: Simple and motivational
body:
We all have a million things to do, but if you're like me, the "routine" can take a back seat to the stuff the pops up in your life, causing you to forget to get things done. 
Enter Swipe. From
Walking the dogs to reminding me to call a friend, this app has a gentle reminder to nudge you back on track. I also like that it syncs up with the Apple Watch so it can track my steps during the day. I love it.
author: shoepershopper

title: Best of its kind
body: Does what it advertises better than any other app. I use it every day.  Zero complaints or qualms; it's perfect.
author: EvilTKat

title: Clean and simple, exactly what I wanted
body: I love the simplicity of this app. You add a streak and then just tap it every day as you finish it. It also interfaces with Apple health so you can have a streak for so many steps or miles per day and it auto-tracks it for you. Love it.
author: MissWhich

title: Great app.
body: This app is very handy. It helps keep me on track. And the Apple Watch app is a great companion.
author: skinnybones2013

title: Clean, easy, and motivating interface
body: I primarily use this app from my Watch, and it works great. All the important yet mundane daily tasks of mine I'm that much more cognizant and motivated to complete. Thank you!
author: SeenSaid

title: Amazing app!
body: Thats exactly   what I looked for
author: WhiteRiver

title: Simpler Apple Watch app?
body: The main app is fine - nice and simple. The Apple Watch app though is wonky. The use of force touch makes it awkward to complete tasks. Why not just make it the same as the app?
author: HeyMonkee

title: Great app with a few additions needed
body: The app does exactly what is advertised and the developer was extremely responsive when something strange happened with the Watch interface. A great addition would be the ability to select a custom number of times per day for certain tasks.
author: MtTt1-7-7-6

title: Really simple and useful
body:
I was surprised how simple but useful this app is. Well worth the small price. It's got a lot of small features that are really nice. Even exporting?? Seriously?! That's so cool. 

Thanks for making this!!
author: Giminoshi

title: Winner!
body:
This app is a winner. I love the six dots on my watch face suing the day as a reminder of the things that are important to me. I'm using it in conjunction with the "miracle morning" from Hal Elrod.

My main request is to make it quicker to complete a take on the watch app. Too many steps. Make it a tap in the circle you wannabe complete right on the main screen with all six icons.
author: RodChristiansen

title: Great app
body: Practical app that actually works!
author: Ed Costa Rica

title: My Accountabilibuddy!
body: Streaks is just what I've needed to turn inconsistency into a positive habit.  It's perfect for those things that are easy to do & also easy not to do.  Streaks is my motivator and gives me that push when I try to put something off, to just do it!
author: sandy98403

title: Great app
body: Nice to see my consistency over time. There is some lag in updating the watch app, usually need to open the app on the phone for new data like steps, flights of stairs to sync over to the watch.
author: Jake the Jake

title: Not Worth $3.99
body: I have an Apple Watch and was excited about getting this app due to its compatibility with the watch. Unfortunately, I don't feel it does anything different than the free reminders app that comes with my phone. If given the option I would take a refund :-/
author: KatMarBat

title: Love this app
body: This app is great! I'm also very happy at how fast the developer took advantage of Apple Watch complications. The only thing that I need is the ability to track multi-actions/day, such as: brushing teeth twice a day, drinking 8 glasses of water, taking vitamins/supplements twice a day. Otherwise, this app has been very helpful for motivation. I look forward to completing the circles and getting all six.
author: Sleep tech 67

title: Perfect example of app development
body:
When you think of it, a simple checklist or reminder app should do they same thing Streaks does. Just set a recurring task and do it every day. But that's not how our (or my) brain works. Streaks takes brilliant advantage of our desire to keep a streak going as well as the bizarre yet effective method of the quantified self. You'll find yourself wanting to keep that streak alive, and frustrated when you don't. 

My nits are all incredibly minor visual points. Nothing that distracts from the overall goal of the app. This is a great example of an app you never knew you needed until you tried it. Well worth a couple bucks.
author: Brizzzad

title: Well-Considered and Thoughtful App
body: I've been using Streaks for just about a week, and am finding that it nudges me toward good habits, much like Apple Watch’s activity rings.
author: BeautymarkStudio

title: An excellent example of the power of gamification.
body: This app looks great (color options, yay!) and is strangely compelling. It's a great tool to help build new habits. I'm finding myself eerily obsessed with keeping my streaks going. A worthwhile investment.
author: breebearrr

title: Great App for habitual/daily tasks
body:
The app needs one more feature that I would love to become efficient:

- The ability to "undo" and "edit" a streak. Sometimes I accidentally add a street for the wrong day.
author: JohnKnee Appleseed

title: Well-thought out and cleanly implemented
body: Very well done overall. Easy to use UI and great concept. Every other similar app is missing some key functionality but this one is not. The only possibly complaint count be that 6 habits is too few but simplicity is the point in this regard. Also the best 3rd party watch app that I have so far as well and the only 3rd party app I've found that offers a complication that works well, both in a technical sense and in the sense that it adds useful info to my watch face.
author: AveryMBarr

title: Very thoughtful
body:
I love the simple design, but there are a lot of thoughtful and nuanced features as well. It notices when you're failing to meet goals consistently, offers to let you mark a task from the day before in case you forgot, and just feels good to wear. 

The Watch App is also nice, and the complication increases the overall usefulness.
author: Beautyislikeyeah

title: Good
body: Simple and effective. Not many bells and whistles. Watch complication is nice.
author: Dagonis

title: Good habit former
body: Has helped me a lot.
author: Figure 88

title: Simple, Fun, and Effective Habit Tracker
body:
Ive made Streaks my habit tracker for the last week and it has been great. 

I used to struggle with motivating myself to use a habit tracker. But Streaks has made it simple and easy. 

Great beautiful design makes me want to open the app or Apple Watch face complication and get my habits in. 

Enjoying every update and look forward to making more great habits.
author: mrarlen

title: It Works!
body: This app is simple to use and really does motivate you to achieve your goals. Recommended.
author: shockmeee

title: Habits
body: Apps - or any mobile website application or interface - should consider psychology and aim to build an experience that creates or enables positive habits. Streaks is simple and simply the best for developing, measuring, maintaining and improving on habitual action.
author: Emogil7

title: Simple app, clean UI
body: Great app and gets the job done. App Store needs more simple apps like this one.
author: hkareem2222

title: Simple and effective.
body:
This habit building app is the best one I've used for the way my brain works.  The big circles are satisfying to check off, and I like the layout.

If given the option to add indefinite habits, I would have a ton of them and set myself up for failure.
author: zofiava

title: Great
body: I've used them all. I keep using this one. Simple and efficient design. Some people don't like the fact that you can only track six habits. I actually think it is a strength. I can focus on fewer habits more effectively than many and with higher success.
author: C4 mailman

title: Staying on the edge of technology
body:
Good job taking advantage of the latest features! I'm really pleased with the watch OS2 complications this app has. Great way to remind me of my goals at a glance.

The app itself has great features too. Love that you can set a separate reminder for each goal throughout the day.

Worth the price!
author: Mattpizza

title: Good app with 2 major shortcomings...
body:
1. You can’t set your habits to a certain number of times per week. You are restricted to doing them on set days per week. There are so many competing apps that allow this feature.

2. You are limited to only 6 habits. If you want to set more habits you’re out of luck. There are so many competing apps that allow the user to set the quantity of habits that they want.

This app has so much potential but I would wait to buy until these features are added. It’s a well designed app that’s easy to use.
author: Do It Now

title: Perfection
body: A few things to do each day. Meditate or Walk or Study. Apple Watch support too? Excellent.
author: Karlwireless

title: Clean, simple and delivers
body: The app is easy to use with an easy interface and does what it promises well.
author: evidisson

title: Super helpful!
body:
Excellent app. My amateur research on habit-building informs my opinion. Feels good to use it. I appreciate that it restricts me to six habits. Otherwise it would be too tempting to overwhelm myself with more demands and expectations. It's forced me to focus on building a few small habits-- starting small-- which shows much more self-compassion.

I wish the icons were better-organized, that there were more variety of hygiene and time icons, and that you could color-code your habits.

I love that I can set reminder times individually. I wish I could set different times for different days to account for varying daily schedules.
author: The Bob Loblaw Law Blog

title: Awesome
body: Favorite goal-related app. Love the layout, very simple. Very aesthetically pleasing
author: Ashybashy95

title: Great and well thought out app
body: I really like how much this app respects the user.
author: richarmstrong

title: Great app
body: This app does exactly what it says it does, and helps me greatly. It is a reminder to work on a goal that is simple or profound, it is up to the user. It is well worth the money and from what I understand, the developer is removing the social media restriction.
author: Cynwr58

title: Great app
body: I've tried a few habit trackers before, but always stopped using them after a couple of days. Streaks is  the first habit tracker I have used for 8+ consecutive weeks now. It's a simple, beautifully designed and easy to use habit tracker. I recommend the in-app purchase.
author: the-ocean

title: I give up
body:
I like this app.  The price is ok for what it is.  I have actually developed better habits because of this apps simplicity.  I kind of wish there was an option to have different levels of goals, like six more would appear when, and only when, the first six were met.

I hope this review will somehow make the app stop asking me to leave my uninspired, uninformed feedback for the rest of the world to read.  

Buy this app if you're the kind of person who doesn't accomplish much as the result of setting too many goals.  Also, if you realize that 4 or 5 dollars probably amounts to nothing when you consider how long it probably took to learn how to make apps and then actually make this app.  

Donald Trump 2016!!! Just kidding.  Wouldn't that be horrible???
author: crashman1203

title: Very Cool Twist on Achieving Goals
body: Very cool twist on a productivity app to help you in achieving your goals. There seems to be something missing, but I can't quite put my finger on it. The app could be more engaging for the user otherwise a very good goal tracking app
author: Surge55

title: Love the app, not a fan of the updates
body: This app is by far my favorite habit tracking. It easy to use and has a great feature where you can easily see you streaks. However, I'm not a fan of sharing on social media to get upgrades or a $4 price tag.
author: rannauk

title: Solid
body: App does what it is intended to do. I have no issues.
author: Fresh2284

title: Simple
body: Simple and fast makes it easy to use everyday. It increases your wish to create and keep good habits
author: 2204bbc

title: !! Misleading: New features are locked !!
body:
Update: $4 for a simple (limited) app and new features are now locked and require sharing via social media to unlock. The developer doesn't mention this is the apps details. Hopefully this isn't the model they'll use for future feature enhancements.

Simple and intuitive way to track goals wrapped in a beautiful interface. The developer listens and responds quickly, adding features and improvements.
author: Jrcaban

title: Hey, I encourage you to use this app
body:
Streaks is simple to understand and use. I appreciate that only six events can be held at a time. This prompts me to consider what is truly a priority in my day. However, the app is, of course, only helpful and effective based on the streaker's personal drive to change. 

I like that it only notifies you once in the evening and only if you have used the app that day. Also that the notification symbol reflects how many streaks are left to accomplish. 

Cool idea and excellent execution.
author: Cool Guy Y'all Ready Kno

title: Very effective app, a few limitations
body:
First, the interface couldn't be easier to figure out and use. The app feels and looks very professionally done. There are some limitations, though. I'm using it to track a steps per day goal. There is no manual way of adding steps, because it uses the built-in step counter. This means if you went for a walk without your phone (or Apple Watch), they can't be counted. Also, setting the step goal is in increments of 1,000. What if I want to set a goal of 2,500?

Anyway, with those limitations in mind, it's still a very good "don't break the chain" goal tracker.
author: runester

title: Just started a small business
body: This helps me so much to keep my day moving and to keep me sane with so many things going on!!
author: Kenan wang

title: Really useful app!!
body: Does exactly what it says. No app will change your life, but this is a useful tool for trying to better yourself.
author: Blond3Man

title: Great app for any daily/weekly reminders
body: From banal tasks like take out the trash to fairly complicated life goals this is a good simple way to mark them. Love the interface. Wish this company would make a nice clean, easy to use medication reminder app!
author: bonzoid1957

title: Great for forming habits!
body: This app has been really awesome so far. I like how it helps me to think of my goals day by day, one day at a time. Since using this app, I really have seen an improvement in my motivation and success to fulfill seemingly mundane daily tasks that I need to accomplish. Streaks helps tasks feel doable. I also love that it helps me feel accomplished when I get to mark something off!
author: Magsnidget

title: Easy to Use, Great Design
body: I've been using this app for a few weeks and have been pleased with it so far. It's beautifully simple with great design.
author: Buzz Wrightyear

title: Amazing
body: I don't know why this works but the satisfaction of holding down a task and seeing the circle fill up makes you want to complete the task. A++
author: vckyw

title: Almost There!
body: I love the simplicity of this app's elegant design but it needs more robust functionality. Currently it only allows six trackable 'streaks.' I need more and strongly suspect others do, too. While limiting the number of available tasks is helpful because it encourages realistic and focused goal-setting, I suggest increasing the task limit to ten. Also, we need more customization. It's great that week can customize task reminders but I have some tasks that need to be executed more than once a day to be considered legitimate finished and therefore legitimately part of a streak (for instance I need to check my planner in the morning, afternoon, and evening). Likewise, as an example, people have to take medications more than once a day but probably don't want to create different tasks for different medications so they would want a single 'take medication' streak but with multiple customizable reminders. Ideally the task could include incremental sub-checkboxes for each increment of completion and the user could ultimately only mark the streak complete once all the checkboxes were filled (and allow the app to keep track in case they want to go back and see the details of any unfulfilled streaks, so they could see that maybe one day of the month they only checked two out of three of the checkboxes). Anyway I sincerely love the potential of this app and its beautiful design but the beauty and simplicity can be maintained even if you make the app more practical and functional.

title: More Icons Please
body:
I love the simplicity of the interface and have been using the app for a month now. It's definitely helping me be mindful of the habits I'm trying to form. Three things I would like to modify if I could:
1. More icon options please 
2. A better completion satisfaction screen. If I have a task that is not a daily one (every other day of the week) and I complete all the 5 other tasks for that day, I don't get a completion screen, even though there are only 5 tasks instead of 6 for that day. I think it would be nice to have that visual reward to keep you going. Maybe a "great job, you're on a streak" message and a change of color of the screen. We all like to feel we have accomplished something. 
3. More in app suggestions I liked that after being on a streak with the amount of steps I take a day, the app asked if I wanted to increase the steps to take me to the next level. I liked that and would like to see that sort of suggestion for other tasks.

title: Exactly what I wanted and nothing more
body: The app is beautiful, simple and does exactly what it needs to without any fluff. I always get annoyed when apps add extra bells and whistles that just get in your way. I also really like that it uses the badge number to remind you there are still things to be done. For someone with mild OCD like myself, clearing that badge icon is a big motivator to do the things on my list. It's also great that it allows you to check off the previous day in case you forgot. Admittedly, it seems a tad overpriced, but I personally feel it's a small price to pay since it actually helps me build good habits. For the price of a single cappuccino I am actually improving my life!
